research_rationale: Identity: the held Federal Register text (13 FR 6104, the issue of October 19, 1948; the order begins on PDF page 6 and its attached lists continue on page 7) is the order itself: it is headed Executive Order 10010, creates an emergency board under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act for the Akron & Barberton Belt Railroad Company dispute, and is signed by Harry S. Truman at The White House on October 18, 1948. I read the whole order; the representation is the machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, and I did not inspect the page images. End: express revocation by Executive Order 12553 on 1986-02-25, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines (option C): a report deadline and a spent standstill are not ends. Prior research: a filed claim for this order exists (research/readiness/claims/claude-2026-10-31-apollo-g03.jsonl, line 11) and carries an independent AI whole-case review, but its reasoning described Executive Order 10015 as an amendment without recording it as a later event with a source; this version records it from the Federal Register text of Executive Order 10015 and keeps the end date. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete with no coverage warning and no scope note. The U.S. Code and eCFR searches found no hit naming this order; the Federal Register catalog search found the two instruments recorded here (the amendment of November 5, 1948 and the revocation of February 25, 1986).
savings_reason: Executive Order 12553, read in full, contains no saving or transition provision: its text is one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders, an editorial note and the signature block. The commands of this order were one-time commands tied to one railway labor dispute, and no held claim-grade source shows any of them continuing when it was revoked. The statute the order applied, section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160), is a separate source of law and does not depend on this order.
earlier_end_check: The order contains no fixed end date and no termination clause. Its commands are a bar on interested board members, a requirement that the board report within thirty days from the date of the order (due by November 17, 1948), and a standstill that runs from the date of the order until thirty days after the report. The report deadline and the standstill are spent facts, not ends, under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 on report deadlines, and neither is claimed as the end. A held lead copy of the board's own report (a text of PDF pages 1-8 of 70 from the National Mediation Board site, graded held_text_lead, a grade the claim format does not accept as a cited source) carries the date December 17, 1948 on its title page and states that the parties stipulated on the record to extend the time for the board to submit its report to the President until December 17; thirty days after December 17, 1948 is January 16, 1949. These dates are leads and are not recorded as later events, because no claim-grade source and no reviewed factual-event record for the report is held for this order; they are also not claimed as an end, and the clause is described only as functionally spent. The dossier chain, the Federal Register catalog disposition note for this order (amended by Executive Order 10015 of November 5, 1948; revoked by Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986) and my reading of the held texts of Executive Order 10015 and Executive Order 12553 show no revoking, superseding or terminating instrument before 1986-02-25. Executive Order 10015 is an amendment of the attached lists and is recorded as a later event, not as an end.
scope_check: One clause is inventoried: the operative text from the order heading through the standstill sentence (the recitals, the creation of the board of three members, the bar on interested members, the thirty-day report requirement and the standstill). The signature, the date line and the attached List A and List B follow it. The recitals incorporate the lists by reference to identify the carriers and the railway labor organizations, and the lists contain no command; Executive Order 10015 later amended them. Executive Order 12553 revokes the order by number as a whole, not in part, so every command in the clause ends on the same date. The ending source cited is the revoking sentence of Executive Order 12553.
independent_command_check: Each command (create the board, bar interested members, require the report, freeze conditions) depends on this order and on the dispute it created; none is a separate delegation, continuing regulation or standing rule. The standstill sentence applies section 10 of the Railway Labor Act (45 U.S.C. 160); the statute is a separate source of law that an Executive order does not revoke, but the periods it measures here were set by this order's creation of the board, and no held claim-grade source shows them still running when the order was revoked.
savings_check: Executive Order 12553 was read in full: it consists of one revoking sentence, a table of the revoked orders by number and subject, an editorial note and the signature block, and it contains no saving or transition provision. No residual effect of this order is shown to depend on its continued force. Savings state none_after_bounded_search; section 10 of the Railway Labor Act continues independently as stated in the independent-command check.
